testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
Remove wheel chocks and release the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal quickly several times.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test it by pressing and releasing the brake pedal quickly. This releases air from the brakes. The warning signal should turn on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual air brakes, a leak in one system ____ the second system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. If one system leaks, it may not affect the other system.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil sometimes appear in the compressed air of an air brake system. These substances:

options.text: Are needed for the system to work properly.
Should make up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil can damage the air brake system if they build up. Air tanks have drains to remove this buildup. You should open manual drains at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: A ____ between the air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from leaking out if the compressor breaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be between the air compressor and the first main tank. This valve stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. Because air pressure can leak away, these brakes must use mechanical force to hold.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended:

options.text: Lower the windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Stop right away and park where you are.
Leave the roadway safely as soon as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the roadway safely as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving, safely exit the roadway as soon as you can and park. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The parts that stop the vehicle are inside the drum brake.

questions.question: In a single air system, air pressure should build up within:
questions.explanation: In single air systems, pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in three minutes.

questions.question: In an applied leakage test, the maximum air loss for a triple combination vehicle is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: Know the safe maximum air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination vehicle should lose no more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air gets pumped into the storage tanks. It stops pumping when pressure gets too high. It starts pumping when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, make sure that the ____ come on automatically when air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should come on automatically when air tank pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, block the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal on and off. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve will pop out and spring brakes will activate.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system is very low on pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work at all.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one system loses pressure. If air pressure in either tank gets too low while driving, pull over and park right away.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking power.
Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Are not effective on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works together with a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease braking power. ABS only activates when the vehicle's wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not recommended on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
Is one air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Has one system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. Usually one system operates the rear brakes and the other operates the front brakes.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve in the air brake system releases air:

options.text: The air pressure is too high.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air pressure is too high.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air from the tanks when pressure gets too high. If this valve is releasing air, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: What color light indicates a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS use a yellow light to warn drivers of ABS problems.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to function.
questions.explanation: Air brakes work using compressed air.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator is especially important:
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, what does it do?

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns. It pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: While driving, what holds spring brakes in place?
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve releases air from the air brake system, what does this mean?

options.text: There is something wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is something wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air if pressure gets too high. If this happens, something is wrong with the system and a mechanic should check it.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: Only when it is wet outside.

questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and compressor oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tank completely when using the drain.

questions.question: If you brake on dry pavement at 55 mph, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.
